sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic aAccident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 16-08-2022 at about 1:00 p.m., the petitioner had been to Yelahanka to bring homeopathy medicine on his Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-HH-9496.
After taking medicine, when he was returning to his home by riding his motorcycle on the left side of the road, by observing all traffic rules and regulations, on B.B. Main road, near Yelahanka bypass, a Access Scooter bearing No.KA-50-EH-0292, being ridden by its rider in high speed, in rash and negligent manner, came from Hebbal side and dashed to motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident,
he was shifted to Shushrusha Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Apurva Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in- patient.

Earlier to the accident, he was working as H. R.
Generalist, at Kargo EX Logistic Private Limited and was earning a sum of Rs.38,133/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Yelahanka Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said scooter for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of vehicle bearing No. KA-50-EH- 0292 and its validity as on the date of accident.

It has contended that, at the time of alleged accident, the rider of Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-HH-9496 was not holding valid driving licence and without competence to ride the said motorcycle, he rode the same in rash and negligent manner and hit the insured vehicle bearing No.KA-50-EH- 0292 and caused Thipparaju .N vs Manjula on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109581407/
2 the alleged accident.

It has contended that, by considering the damages stated in the M.V.A. report,
it is clearly substantiated that, there is gross negligence on the part of the rider of Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle bearing No.KA-04- HH-9496.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

It has contended that,
the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(C) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries due to the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 16-08-2022 at about 1.00 p.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of Access Scooter, bearing registration No.
KA-50-EH-0292 ?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?
6. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 26 documents as Ex.P.1 to 26.
Further, he has got examined two more witnesses namely Subramanya and Dr. S.A. Somashekara as P.W.2 and P.W.3 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 16-08-2022 at about 1:00 p.m., when the petitioner was returning to his home from Yelahanka on his Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-HH-9496, riding the said vehicle on the left side of the road

, on B.B. Main road, near Yelahanka bypass, the offending scooter bearing No.KA-50- EH-0292, came from Hebbal side in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as H.R. Generalist at Kargo EX Logistic Thipparaju .N vs Manjula on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109581407/
3 Private Limited and earning a sum of Rs.38,133/- per month.

entities.text: Kargo EX Logistic Thipparaju .N vs Manjula
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 26 documents as Ex.P.1 to 26.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 and 6 are true copies of Motor Vehicle Accident reports, Ex.P.7 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.9 is true copy of statement, Ex.P.10 is true copy of notice U/Sec.133 of M.V.
Act, Ex.P.11 is true copy of reply to said notice, Ex.P.12 is discharge summary, Ex.P.13 are medical bills (total 11), Ex.P.14 are prescriptions (total 7), Ex.P15 is notarised copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.16 are X-rays (total 2), Ex.P.17 to 19 are salary slips (total 3), Ex.P.20 is termination letter, Ex.P.21 is authorization letter, Ex.P.22 is notarised copy of MLC register copy, Ex.P.23 is notarised copy of police intimation, Ex.P.24 is inpatient case-sheet, Ex.P.25 is OP record and Ex.P.26 is X-ray.

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 11, prima-facia it reveals that, on 16-08-2022 at about 1:00 p.m., when the petitioner was returning to his home from Yelahanka on his Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-HH-9496, riding the said vehicle on the left side of the road, on B.B. Main road, near Yelahanka bypass, the offending scooter bearing No.KA-50-EH-0292, came from Hebbal side in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the offending scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-50-EH-0292.
12.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 with respect to scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-50-EH-0292 and its validity as on the date of accident are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company,
though has specifically denied the above stated facts in its written statement and taken specific defence that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving on the part of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-HH-9496 and hitting the same to the scooter bearing No. KA-5-EH-0292 and the pettioner was not holding valid driving licence to ride the said vehicle, it has not produced any evidence to establish the said contentions or any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Even, the respondent No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the contentions taken in its written statement on oath.
The petitioner/P.W.1, has unequivocally denied all the suggestion made in the cross-examination by the learned counsel for respondent No.2.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his Thipparaju .N vs Manjula on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109581407/
4 mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the said accident has caused due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner and there was no negligence on the part rider of offending scooter bearing No. KA-5-EH-0292.
13.

Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 40 feet width Bengaluru-Bellary National High, near Yelahanka bypass road, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, due to head collusion of motorcycle of the petitioner proceeding from Yelahaka side and the offending scooter bearing No. KA-5-EH-0292, coming form Hebbal side.

Further, the damage to both the vehicles, as noted in the Ex.P.5 & 6 Motor Vehicle Accident Reports,
clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place due to head collusion of both the vehicles.
14. Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Reports, which are marked as Ex.P.5 and 6, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there is no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending scooter.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of petitioner himself or there was some contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner also in the cause of accident.
Further, the Ex.P.8 final report/chare-sheet filed by the investigation officer has not been challenged by the owner or the rider of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident 15.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.12 discharge summary, Ex.P.24 inpatient case sheet, Ex.P.25 OP record and Ex.P.26 x-ray, it clearly reveals that,
the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered left clavicle distal third fracture.
The same is deposed by P.W.3, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.2, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-50-EH-0292.
16.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

SCC 635
entities.label: PRECEDENT

Thipparaju .N vs Manjula on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109581407/
5 17.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 16-08-2022 at about 1:00 p.m., on B.B. Main road, near Yelahanka bypass, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-50-EH-0292.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-50-EH-0292 and he has sustained left clavicle distal third fracture and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.15.
As per Ex.P.15, the date of birth of the petitioner is 17-04-1994.
The accident has taken place on 16-08-2022 at about 1:00 p.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 28 years.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered left clavicle distal third fracture.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has 25% physical disability of left upper limb and 13%
physical disability for the whole body.
The oral evidence of P.W.3 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.12 discharge summary, Ex.P.24 inpatient case sheet, Ex.P.25 OP record and Ex.P.26 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered left clavicle distal third fracture.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.
Further he has denied that, there are no restrictions of movements to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 16-08-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 18-01- 2024, which is after lapse Thipparaju .N vs Manjula on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109581407/
6 of one year and five months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the lateral end of clavicle fracture is united with implants in situ.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as H.R.
Generalist at Kargo EX Logistic Private Limited and earning a sum of Rs.38,133/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do centering work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
To substantiate the same he has produced salary slips and termination letter as per Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.20.
But, he has not examined the author of those documents.
The petitioner has failed to establish his income as on the date of accident, through cogent and corroborative evidence.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 28 years is 17.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 8/100 X 17 = Rs.2,52,960/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 11 medical bills, as per Ex.P.13.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.87,714/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.87,714/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
suffered left clavicle distal third fracture.
As per Ex.P.12 discharge summary
, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 04 days from 16-08-2022 to 19-08-2022, in Apurva Mother and Child Hospital, Bengaluru.

entities.text: Apurva Mother and Child Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further, as per P.W.3, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner,
this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

Bengaluru.

vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Kodigenahalli Hobli, Madhugiri Taluk,
Gutte, Tumkur, the accident has taken place on B.B. Main road, near Yelahanka Bypass, Bengaluru and the petitioner has taken treatment at Apurva Mother and Child Hospital, Bengaluru.

vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 4 days as inpatient at Apurva Mother and Child Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.

entities.label: ORG

Therefore,
Rs.15,500 x 2 = Rs.31,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:
It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 28 years and unfortunately he has suffered left clavicle distal third fracture.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 8% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.40,000/-.
The P.W.3 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery or for further treatment.

Therefore,
this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,52,960-00 2.
Medical expenses 87,714-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 4,000-00 Thipparaju .N vs Manjula on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109581407/
8 5. Food and nourishment 3,200-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 2,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period
8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Tota Rs. 4,60,874-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,60,874/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
21. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 is the insurer and respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-50-EH-0292 the said accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,60,874/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.4,60,874/- (Rupees four lakh sixty thousand eight hundred and seventy four only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to Thipparaju .N vs Manjula on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109581407/

draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident 15.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the lateral end of clavicle fracture is united with implants in situ.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
To substantiate the same he has produced salary slips and termination letter as per Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.20.
But, he has not examined the author of those documents.
The petitioner has failed to establish his income as on the date of accident, through cogent and corroborative evidence.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore,
this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.
20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,52,960-00 2.
Medical expenses 87,714-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4.
Conveyance expenses 2,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period
8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00 9.
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,60,874/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,60,874/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.4,60,874/- (Rupees four lakh sixty thousand eight hundred and seventy four only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
